g.text: Three stores, three shapes - and the system reuses its own primitive for one of them
The row that decides everything is MUTABILITY: messages are written once, offsets are overwritten thousands of times a second.
Storing offsets in a plain append-only log would mean the log grows without bound while holding one useful value per key -
you would retain a million historical positions for a group that only needs its current one.
Compaction: retention becomes 'keep the latest value per key'
This gives a key-value store built out of the log - and it fits the offset workload precisely:
a commit is still a sequential APPEND, so it inherits the whole 244x advantage
size becomes proportional to the number of DISTINCT KEYS, not the number of writes
it is a topic, so it gets ISR replication and leader election with no new machinery
recovery is a log replay, and compaction is what makes that replay bounded
The elegance: the system reuses its own primitive to store its own
state. A database table would be the right SHAPE and would make
every commit a random write - forfeiting the sequential advantage
the whole design is built on.
Why __consumer_offsets is keyed on group_id ALONE
All of a group's offsets live in ONE partition - the same partition whose
leader hosts that group's coordinator. Three things fall out at once:
a coordinator reads only ITS OWN partition to recover a group
finding the coordinator needs no lookup service: hash the group name
a group's commits are TOTALLY ORDERED, which is what makes the
generation-ID fencing meaningful - a stale commit is unambiguously stale
Keying on (group_id, topic, partition) instead would spread one group's offsets
across all 50 partitions, forcing a coordinator to read every partition on
recovery AND destroying the ordering that fencing relies on. Key selection is
doing the same load-bearing work as shard-key selection in a database.
Why the cluster map canNOT also be a compacted topic
Bootstrapping. The map tells you which broker leads which partition - storing it
in a partition means needing the map to find the map. And it needs linearizable
consensus with leader election and ephemeral sessions, which ISR replication
gives durability for but not 'exactly one controller, and everyone agrees who'.
